Record Class StreamingUploadOptions

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.streaming.StreamingUploadOptions
Record Components:
engageAboveBytes - only request bodies larger than this are split; smaller ones are passed through byte for byte, so that ordinary requests behave exactly as they do without the filter. This is measured on the whole request body, i.e. metadata plus the base64 of all documents in it.
memoryThresholdBytes - extracted document content up to this size is kept in memory instead of being written to a temporary file. This is measured on a single decoded document and is therefore deliberately independent of engageAboveBytes; it is quite normal for it to be the larger of the two. Splitting the body is what avoids the expensive part — the base64 text and the decoded array that the FHIR parser would otherwise materialize — whereas a temporary file is only needed to also avoid a large contiguous heap allocation. Small documents therefore stay in memory and cause no disk I/O at all.
maxDocumentSizeBytes - maximum size of a single extracted document. Bounds how much temporary disk space one request can use.
tempDirectory - directory for temporary document files
inlineDocumentResources - types of the resources whose create interaction carries a document inline, i.e. the resource types below the FHIR base for which a POST is a candidate for the split. A POST to the FHIR base itself always is one, because a transaction bundle may contain anything. See MHD_INLINE_DOCUMENT_RESOURCES for the value that covers MHD.
public record StreamingUploadOptions(int engageAboveBytes, int memoryThresholdBytes, long maxDocumentSizeBytes, Path tempDirectory, Set<String> inlineDocumentResources) extends Record
Settings of the streaming upload split, see Base64SplittingFilter.

These are the only settings the split needs; whether it is active at all, and where the values come from, is up to whoever registers the filter. The defaults are meant to be usable as they are — see defaults().

    • MHD_INLINE_DOCUMENT_RESOURCES

      public static final Set<String> MHD_INLINE_DOCUMENT_RESOURCES
      The resource types that carry a document inline in MHD: only ITI-105 does, as a DocumentReference with the document in content.attachment.data. ITI-65 arrives as a transaction bundle posted to the FHIR base instead and is therefore covered without being named here. The remaining MHD transactions that accept a DocumentReference body — the ITI-57 based updates — are metadata-only, so they are of no interest here even though they are uploads.
